title: Introduce shadow-prefetch probe and SKU-aware trace attribution
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Long-tail cost/latency incidents often arise from ineffective prefetch or background warmup strategies and from which SKU (model variant / quantization tier / hardware class) paid for the tokens. Existing observability surfaces show token-level cost and latency but do not connect synthetic prefetch effectiveness to SKU-level charge attribution. This PR adds a shadow-prefetch probe that issues lightweight synthetic invocations alongside production traffic (opt-in per-deployment) and stitches their traces into the real invocation graph to measure warmup effectiveness and per-SKU cost origins.

Design summary: - Shadow-prefetch probe service (telemetry/shadow_probe) that generates controlled mini-invocations matching recent prompt shapes; results are emitted as synthetic spans and a compact summary event. - SKU-aware tagging: spans created by the runtime now include a compact "sku.id" tag (string) and an inferred "sku.reason" label when fallbacks/quantization happen. These tags are propagated through the trace envelope and included in cost-attribution rollups. - Trace stitching: a new lightweight indexer joins synthetic spans to production traces via a shared correlation token (X-Trace-Anchor) without exposing user payloads. The join is privacy-preserving: only span metadata and aggregated counters are emitted to observability backends. - Dashboard: new panels under Observability -> Prefetch Effectiveness showing: synthetic warmup success rate, delta in first-token latency when warmup succeeded vs not, SKU cost slices, and a microbudget sparkline per-tenant. - Alerts: add a tuned SLO alert rule that triggers when the synthetic warmup success rate drops >20% for a tenant or when SKU-cost-per-token shifts by +30% relative to a trailing baseline. Alerts use a 5m lookback with a 3x hysteresis to avoid churn.

Backward compatibility and opt-in: Shadow-prefetch probe is disabled by default; customers enable per-deployment via the existing observability config (observe.prefetch.enable=true). SKU tags are additive string labels that do not change existing metric names. The trace-stitching indexer can be deployed in the private control plane for Private customers; default behaviour in hosted is to emit aggregated counters only.

Testing and validation: Unit tests added for trace tag propagation and synthetic span generation. End-to-end harness (tests/e2e/prefetch_harness) simulates varying prompt shapes and hardware fallbacks; we ran the harness against a dedicated staging pool for 48h. Performance bench: shadow probe adds <1% request overhead on a 1k RPS staging cluster when enabled. Privacy review: design reviewed by Security (Priya) to ensure no user payloads are leaked; probe emits only aggregated summaries and synthetic span metadata.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag, 2) Enable for internal staging and SRE tenants for 2 weeks, 3) Gradual opt-in to Hosted customers via console toggle + doc update.

Related: references ENG-8142 (linear) for the initial post-incident analysis and SUP-412 for the customer request.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation and unit tests - [x] E2E harness + perf run - [x] Security review - [x] Dashboard and alert rules - [x] Docs stub and console feature flag

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Nice end-to-end. Two asks: (1) make the probe opt-in at deployment level, (2) add a rate-limiter so we don't create synthetic bursts that distort autoscaling. Please add tests for rate-limiting behavior.
Maya Chen (author): added rate limiter to probe (token-bucket) and wired a deployment-level opt-in flag. Added unit test covering limiter edge cases.
Priya Nair: Security review done. Confirmed no payload leak; recommend explicit doc note about privacy guarantees. Added doc note in docs/observability/prefetch-probe.md.

Diego Ramos: Observability nit - the SKU tag cardinality looks bounded but add an allowlist config for hosted. Author updated to include sku.allowlist in config and fallthrough to 'unknown' for unknown SKUs.
Liam O'Connor: CI flakes on unit-tests re-run; reran and all checks green. Approving in comments.
release_notes: Add opt-in shadow-prefetch probe that generates synthetic warmup invocations, SKU-aware trace tags for cost attribution, new Observability dashboard panels for prefetch effectiveness, and tuned alerts for warmup failure and SKU cost shifts.
